method: keyword-only select with a volume floor, so each row costs 11 units rather than 22. The question asked of each probe was not 'does this pattern have demand' but 'does the demand carry the MODIFIER the shape needs' - a city name, a neighbourhood name, a cuisine, an attribute. A pattern with large national volume and no city-scoped variants cannot support one page per city.

probes.evidence: 195 keywords, but the shape of them is brand ('is john lewis open on easter sunday', 'what time does tesco open on sunday') or 'near me', which is a local-pack query and not a page. Generic class-level national queries exist ('supermarkets open on sunday', 'pharmacies open on sunday', 'post offices open on sunday'). City-qualified variants: none in the top 195.
probes.consequence: city_opening is NOT justified per city in this market. Restricted to large cities only, and the rest is recorded as rejected rather than generated.

probes.evidence: Fewer keywords than the UK but genuinely city-qualified: 'supermarkt münchen sonntag geöffnet', 'apotheke berlin sonntag geöffnet', 'bäckerei chemnitz sonntag geöffnet', 'bäcker magdeburg sonntag geöffnet', 'friseur münchen sonntag geöffnet', 'bäcker wolfsburg sonntag geöffnet', 'bäckerei bayreuth sonntag geöffnet', 'bäcker zwickau sonntag geöffnet'. Sunday closing is a legal institution in Germany, which is why the query is city-specific there and not in the UK.
probes.consequence: the shape is validated for de-DE, and Chemnitz, Magdeburg, Wolfsburg, Bayreuth and Zwickau show it reaches well below the largest cities.

probes.evidence: class-level national demand is strong ('supermarché ouvert le dimanche', 'pharmacie ouvert le dimanche', 'restaurant ouvert le dimanche', 'coiffeur ouvert le dimanche', 'tabac ouvert le dimanche') plus 'autour de moi'. Exactly one city-qualified keyword at this floor: 'restaurant rennes ouvert le dimanche'.

one cuisine in one market yields 205 keywords above 100 volume, carrying city modifiers (Milton Keynes, Bristol, Newcastle, Liverpool, Leeds, Oxford, Nottingham, Chelmsford, Norwich, Cheltenham, Lincoln, Watford, Coventry, Preston, Bradford, Slough, St Albans, Bath, York, Chester, Southampton, Cambridge) AND neighbourhood modifiers (Mayfair, Soho, Shoreditch, Canary Wharf, Covent Garden, Kings Cross, Tooting, Wembley, Harrow, Hounslow, East Ham, Blackheath, Brick Lane, Battersea Power Station, Central London, London Bridge).
probes.consequence: the cuisine axis is the strongest aggregation shape measured, and it reaches mid-size cities (Watford and St Albans are around 80-100k) and named neighbourhoods. Not restricted to the largest cities.

probes.evidence: category demand at neighbourhood level is dense for a named area: 'friseur kreuzberg', 'cafe kreuzberg', 'bar kreuzberg', 'kreuzberg bars', 'restaurants kreuzberg', 'restaurant kreuzberg', 'kreuzberg restaurants', 'brunch kreuzberg', 'frühstück kreuzberg', 'kreuzberg essen', 'zahnarzt kreuzberg', 'augenarzt kreuzberg', 'hautarzt kreuzberg', 'kinderarzt kreuzberg', 'massage kreuzberg', 'kreuzberg apotheke', 'hostel berlin kreuzberg', 'hotel berlin kreuzberg', 'flohmarkt kreuzberg', 'schwimmbad kreuzberg', 'freibad kreuzberg', 'kreuzberg sehenswürdigkeiten'.
probes.caution: Kreuzberg is a famous neighbourhood. This probe validates the SHAPE for named, recognised areas; it says nothing about an unnamed suburb, which is why the area shapes now require the place to carry a polygon, a population, a Wikidata item or a Wikipedia article before any page is generated from it.

probes.evidence: every city-qualified keyword at this floor is a major city: Liverpool, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Birmingham, Bristol, Brighton, Leeds, London, Manchester. No mid-size or small city appears.
probes.consequence: attribute pages are gated on city population, unlike cuisine pages.

probes.evidence: every one of the 34 keywords above 400 volume is scoped to a German Land and a year: brückentage hessen 2026, brückentage berlin 2026, brückentage 2026 rlp, brückentage 2026 thüringen, brückentage 2026 nrw, brückentage 2026 bayern, brückentage 2026 saarland, brückentage 2026 sachsen, brückentage 2026 schleswig holstein, brückentage niedersachsen 2026, brückentage 2027 nrw, brückentage 2027 bayern, plus urlaub 2026 planen brückentage.
probes.consequence: the country-level long-weekend family cannot answer these, because which working day bridges to a weekend depends on the regional observances each Land keeps. The derivation was re-run per subdivision over national plus regional holidays, producing 348 bridge plans across 12 countries, 32 of them German (16 Laender x 2 years), and pulse.bridge-days-subdivision was added to FAMILY-MASTER as a measured family.

probes.evidence: one keyword only at a floor of 50. The German-language demand for the 90/180 rule is not expressed as 'rechner'.
probes.consequence: recorded as a rejected tool intent for de-DE rather than built on an assumption. Not evidence about other markets.

probes.evidence: two keywords only: 'cost of living calculator' and 'cost of living calculator uk'.
probes.consequence: the calculator framing is not where the demand is in this market.

probes.evidence: four keywords, and the useful one is 'lebenshaltungskosten usa vergleich deutschland': a COUNTRY PAIR, not a calculator.
probes.consequence: the demand that exists here belongs to the existing country-pair comparison family, not to a new calculator family.

probes.evidence: at a floor of 700 volume, 50 of the 52 keywords are about UK government cost of living PAYMENTS: 'dwp cost of living payment', 'universal credit cost of living payment', 'when will it be paid', 'cost of living payment 2026 uk', 'cost of living crisis'. Only 'cost of living comparison' and 'numbeo cost of living' carry the expat comparison intent Livdar serves.
probes.consequence: this is the most expensive mistake the probe prevented. A family built on the head term would have chased a welfare benefit with pages about moving abroad: high volume, zero relevance, and a SERP owned by gov.uk and the DWP. The phrase is recorded as an intent trap and the family stays scoped to explicit comparison phrasing.

probes.evidence: 70 keywords above 1000 volume, researched in Traditional Chinese rather than translated from English. Taiwanese cities and counties are named directly: 台北, 台中, 高雄, 台南, 花蓮, 宜蘭, 嘉義, 新竹, 桃園, 南投, 澎湖, 台東, 屏東, 基隆, 苗栗, 雲林, 彰化, 新北, plus districts 淡水, 士林, 內湖, 新店, 中壢, 礁溪.
probes.consequence: Taiwan is not a thin market, it is an under-researched one. The modifier set is also a data-backed axis where OSM carries the tag: indoor, fee=no for free, and playground or family attraction types.

probes.evidence: the same probe returns foreign destinations searched FROM Taiwan at the same volume floor: 奶良 Nara, 北海道 Hokkaido, 沖縄 Okinawa, 名古屋 Nagoya, 新寿 Shinjuku, 關西 Kansai, 大阪 Osaka, 東京 Tokyo, 曼谷 Bangkok, 釜山 Busan, 泰國 Thailand, 胡志明市 Ho Chi Minh City, 石垃島 Ishigaki, 泉州 Quanzhou.
probes.consequence: zh-Hant-TW earns destination pages for Japanese, Korean and South East Asian destinations, which the reach file did not previously record. Added to CROSS-LANGUAGE-REACH.csv.

ruleDerived.city_cuisine: city population >= 75,000, because Watford and St Albans carry measured cuisine demand
ruleDerived.area_cuisine: named areas only: the place must carry a polygon, population, Wikidata item or Wikipedia article
ruleDerived.city_opening: city population >= 200,000 everywhere, relaxed to 75,000 for de-DE where the measurement shows the query reaching Zwickau and Bayreuth
ruleDerived.area_attribute and area_opening: the area must carry a Wikidata item or a Wikipedia article, which is a stricter test than for area_category: a modifier page inside an area needs the area itself to be a searched entity
